summary: When a verb has two unstressed pronouns, Italian puts them side by side in a fixed order: the person first, the thing second. The idea that makes it click: the first pronoun changes its vowel (mi, ti, ci, vi, si become me, te, ce, ve, se) and gli or le becomes glie-, glued to the second: me lo dai, te la porto, glielo dico, ce n'è.

subs.label: me lo, te la, ce li, ve le: order and vowel change
subs.focus: Indirect mi / ti / ci / vi together with direct lo / la / li / le before a finite verb: the indirect pronoun comes first and changes i to e, and the two are written as two words: me lo dai, te la porto, ce li manda, ve le spiego; non goes before the whole pair (non te lo dico). The direct member is chosen by the gender and number of the noun, which must be named earlier in the item. Typical errors of English speakers, all wrong for certain: English order (lo mi dai, la ti porto), no vowel change (mi lo dai, ti la porto, ci li manda), one word before the verb (melo dai), only one of the two pronouns where both things are already known and the answer needs both (Mi dai il libro? Sì, ti do.), and the wrong gender or number of the direct member (la chiave: te lo porto). Do not build an error on leaving out the indirect pronoun alone: Sì, lo porto is a possible answer.

subs.label: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele: to him, to her, to them, to you (Lei)
subs.focus: Gli and le both become glie- before lo / la / li / le, written as one word with the direct pronoun: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele. The same four forms serve for to him, to her, to them and formal Lei, so the first half never shows who receives; only the second half changes, with the thing. Typical errors, all wrong for certain: le lo / le la for to her (Le lo do), gli lo without the vowel (gli lo porto), two words (glie lo, gli elo), lelo, the belief that glielo is only for a man and so an invented form for a woman, and the second half matched to the person instead of the thing (the book for Maria: gliela do). For to them, lo do loro is a formal written alternative and is correct: never use it as the wrong sentence, and do not make the learner choose between glielo and loro. Capital Glielo for formal Lei is optional: do not test it.

subs.label: me ne, te ne, gliene, ce ne, ve ne
subs.focus: The same first members before ne: me ne, te ne, ce ne, ve ne as two words, gliene as one word. Ne stands for a part or a number of something named (me ne dai due, gliene porto un po') or for di + thing (ve ne parlo domani, gliene ho parlato, non me ne importa). The decision items should force is ne against lo / la / li / le inside the pair: a number or quantity word left after the verb needs ne (gliene do tre), the whole thing needs the direct pronoun (glieli do tutti). Typical errors, all wrong for certain: mi ne, ti ne, gli ne, glie ne, ne in first position (ne mi dai due), a direct pronoun with a number (te li do tre), and no ne at all with a number (Te do tre). The thing must be named earlier in the item. Agreement of the participle with ne (me ne ha dati due) is scored in participle-agreement: write it correctly but do not build the error on it. Andarsene (me ne vado) belongs to ci-and-ne: do not test it here.

subs.label: Reflexive + direct: me lo metto, se le lava, se lo ricorda
subs.focus: A reflexive verb that also has a direct object (mettersi, togliersi, lavarsi with body parts and clothes, ricordarsi, dimenticarsi, comprarsi, mangiarsi, prepararsi): when the object becomes a pronoun, the reflexive pronoun comes first with the vowel change, and third-person si becomes se: me lo metto, te la togli, se le lava, ce lo ricordiamo, ve li comprate, se lo dimenticano. The reflexive member still matches the subject. Typical errors, all wrong for certain: si lo mette, mi lo metto, lo si mette for he puts it on, a reflexive that does not match the subject (io se lo metto), and dropping the reflexive when the noun becomes a pronoun in a rewrite (Mi metto il cappotto, rewritten as Lo metto, changes the verb). In the passato prossimo the auxiliary stays essere and the participle agrees with the direct pronoun (se l'è messa, me le sono lavate): that belongs to the sub-point participle-and-elision. Use the names of clothes and body parts with their real gender, since the pronoun depends on it (la giacca, il cappello, le mani, i denti).

subs.label: Attached pairs: dirtelo, portarglielo, dandomelo, te lo voglio dire
subs.focus: With an infinitive or a gerund the pair goes after the verb and all is written as one word; the infinitive loses its final e: dirtelo, darmela, portarglielo, parlargliene, mettermelo, dandomelo, dicendoglielo. After a preposition this is the only position (per dirtelo, prima di darglielo, senza dirmelo). With potere, volere, dovere, sapere + infinitive, and with stare + gerund, the pair goes either before the first verb or attached at the end, and both are correct: te lo voglio dire / voglio dirtelo, glielo sto dicendo / sto dicendoglielo. Cloze, order and rewrite items must accept both where both are standard, or fix the position in the task. What is wrong for certain: splitting the pair (ti voglio dirlo, lo voglio dirti), putting it between the two verbs (voglio te lo dire), writing it twice (te lo voglio dirtelo), separate words after the verb (dire te lo, portare glielo, dirmi lo), keeping the e (direglielo), and losing the vowel change when attached (dirtilo, darmilo). Imperative forms (dammelo, diglielo) belong to the topic imperative: do not write them here, not even as distractors.

subs.label: Passato prossimo: gliel'ho data, me li ha portati, se l'è messa
subs.focus: In compound tenses the pair goes before the auxiliary. Singular lo and la are normally elided before forms of avere that begin with a vowel sound (me l'ha dato, te l'ho detto, gliel'ho data, ce l'hanno portata), plural li and le are never elided (me li ha dati, gliele ho date), and the participle agrees with the direct member of the pair, never with the person who receives: la lettera, gliel'ho data, even when the receiver is a man; i libri, me li ha portati, even when a woman speaks. With a reflexive + direct pair the auxiliary is essere and the participle agrees with the direct pronoun: la giacca, se l'è messa; le mani, me le sono lavate. Typical errors, all wrong for certain in standard Italian: an unagreed participle after la / li / le (la lettera gliel'ho dato, i libri me li ha portato), agreement with the receiver (to Maria, il libro: gliel'ho data), elided plural (me l'ha portati, gliel'ho date for le chiavi), the pair after the auxiliary (ho glielo dato), avere with a reflexive pair (se l'ha messa). Writing lo or la in full (me lo ha dato) is accepted in writing: never use it as the error. With gliel'ho + masculine singular nothing shows, so choose feminine or plural things when agreement is the point.

subs.label: ci + direct or ne: ce l'ho, ce lo metto, ce n'è, ce ne sono
subs.focus: Ci meaning there, and the ci of fixed verbs, also becomes ce before lo / la / li / le / ne: ce l'ho, ce li ho, ce le ho for having something with you or owning it, ce lo metto, ce la porto, ce li accompagna for putting or taking something or someone to a place already named, and ce n'è + singular, ce ne sono + plural for there is some, there are some. Typical errors, all wrong for certain: ci l'ho, ci lo metto, ci ne sono, ci n'è, the spelling c'è ne and c'è n'è, lo ci metto, ce n'è with a plural number or plural quantity (ce n'è due), and ce ne sono with a singular (ce ne sono uno). In ce l'ho the direct pronoun matches the thing: la penna, ce l'ho; i biglietti, ce li ho; le chiavi, ce le ho. The bare answer Sì, l'ho is rare in speech but not wrong: do not use it as the error. Farcela (ce la faccio) belongs to ci-and-ne. Ce li manda, where ce is to us, belongs to me-lo-order.

subs.label: Level three only: mi ci trovo, ti ci porto, ci si alza
subs.focus: Level three only. Before ci meaning there, or the ci of volerci and metterci, the pronouns mi / ti keep their i and come first: mi ci trovo bene, ti ci porto io, mi ci vogliono dieci minuti, mi ci abituo. The vowel change happens only before lo, la, li, le and ne. With a reflexive verb used impersonally (one gets up, people get used to it) Italian says ci si + third person singular, never si si: ci si alza presto, ci si abitua, ci si diverte. Typical errors, all wrong for certain in standard Italian: me ci trovo, ci mi trovo, te ci porto, si si alza, si ci alza. Keep to mi ci and ti ci with common verbs (trovarsi, portare, accompagnare, abituarsi, volerci, metterci) and to ci si with common reflexive verbs; avoid vi ci and ci ci, which speakers themselves avoid. Other uses of impersonal si (lo si vede) belong to passive-and-si.

rules.rule: Person first, thing second, and mi / ti / ci / vi change to me / te / ce / ve before lo, la, li, le. Two words before the verb.
rules.pattern: me / te / ce / ve + lo / la / li / le + verb | me lo dai | te la porto | non ve li do

examples.tl: Mi dai il libro? Sì, te lo do subito.
examples.en: Will you give me the book? Yes, I'll give it to you right away.

examples.tl: La chiave te la porto domani.
examples.en: I'll bring you the key tomorrow.

examples.tl: Le foto ce le manda Paolo stasera.
examples.en: Paolo is sending us the photos this evening.

examples.tl: È un segreto: non ve lo dico.
examples.en: It is a secret: I am not telling you.

rules.note: The second pronoun follows the thing: il libro, me lo dai; la penna, me la dai; i soldi, me li dai; le chiavi, me le dai. English often leaves out it (I'll tell you); Italian keeps it: te lo dico.

rules.rule: To him, to her, to them and formal to you are all glie-, glued to the direct pronoun in one word: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele. Le lo does not exist.
rules.pattern: glie + lo / la / li / le + verb | glielo porto | gliela mando | non glieli do

examples.tl: Marco vuole il giornale: glielo porto io.
examples.en: Marco wants the newspaper: I'll take it to him.

examples.tl: Anna aspetta la risposta: gliela mando oggi.
examples.en: Anna is waiting for the answer: I'll send it to her today.

examples.tl: I ragazzi vogliono i biglietti: glieli compro io.
examples.en: The boys want the tickets: I'll buy them for them.

examples.tl: Signora, il conto glielo porto subito.
examples.en: Madam, I'll bring you the bill right away.

rules.note: Only the ending changes, and it follows the thing, not the person: gliela mando can be to him or to her, and la is the answer. For to them, formal writing also has lo do loro.

rules.rule: Before ne the first pronoun changes in the same way: me ne, te ne, ce ne, ve ne, and gliene in one word. Use ne when a number or amount follows, or for di + thing.
rules.pattern: me ne / te ne / gliene + verb + quantity | me ne dai due | gliene parlo

examples.tl: Il vino è buono: me ne dai un po'?
examples.en: The wine is good: will you give me some?

examples.tl: Ho molte mele: te ne regalo tre.
examples.en: I have a lot of apples: I'll give you three.

examples.tl: Luca ama i libri: gliene compro due.
examples.en: Luca loves books: I'll buy him two.

examples.tl: Il viaggio è stato bello: ve ne parlo domani.
examples.en: The trip was lovely: I'll tell you about it tomorrow.

rules.note: All of it is lo / la / li / le, a part of it is ne: i biscotti, glieli porto tutti, but gliene porto quattro.

rules.rule: With a reflexive verb the reflexive pronoun comes first and changes too: me lo, te la, se li, ce le, ve lo. Third-person si becomes se.
rules.pattern: me / te / se / ce / ve + lo / la / li / le + verb | me lo metto | se le lava

examples.tl: Fa freddo: il cappotto me lo metto subito.
examples.en: It is cold: I am putting my coat on right away.

examples.tl: I bambini hanno le mani sporche: se le lavano prima di cena.
examples.en: The children have dirty hands: they wash them before dinner.

examples.tl: Paolo sa il mio nome, ma non se lo ricorda mai.
examples.en: Paolo knows my name, but he never remembers it.

examples.tl: Hai caldo con la giacca? Perché non te la togli?
examples.en: Are you hot in your jacket? Why don't you take it off?

rules.note: The first pronoun still matches the subject: io me lo metto, tu te lo metti, lei se lo mette, noi ce lo mettiamo. Do not drop it: lo metto means I put it somewhere, not I put it on.

rules.rule: After an infinitive or a gerund the pair is attached and everything is one word. The infinitive drops its final e: dire + te lo gives dirtelo.
rules.pattern: infinitive without e + pair | dirtelo | portarglielo | parlargliene | dandomelo

examples.tl: Ho comprato un regalo e vengo per dartelo.
examples.en: I have bought a present and I am coming to give it to you.

examples.tl: Sa la verità, ma è partito senza dirmela.
examples.en: He knows the truth, but he left without telling me.

examples.tl: Dicendoglielo subito, eviti molti problemi.
examples.en: By telling him right away, you avoid a lot of problems.

rules.note: After a preposition (per, di, senza, prima di) the pair can only be attached to the infinitive.

rules.rule: With potere, volere, dovere or sapere + infinitive, put the pair before the first verb or attach it to the infinitive. Both are correct. Never split the pair and never write it twice.
rules.pattern: te lo voglio dire = voglio dirtelo | glielo devo portare = devo portarglielo

examples.tl: Te lo posso spiegare domani.
examples.en: I can explain it to you tomorrow.

examples.tl: Posso spiegartelo domani.
examples.en: I can explain it to you tomorrow.

examples.tl: Non glielo voglio dire adesso.
examples.en: I do not want to tell him now.

examples.tl: Marta aspetta i documenti: devo portarglieli oggi.
examples.en: Marta is waiting for the documents: I have to take them to her today.

rules.note: The same choice exists with stare + gerund: te lo sto dicendo or sto dicendotelo; the first is more usual.

rules.rule: In the passato prossimo the pair goes before avere. Lo and la are normally written l' there, li and le never are, and the participle agrees with the thing: gliel'ho data, me li ha portati.
rules.pattern: pair + avere + participle agreeing with lo / la / li / le | gliel'ho data | me li ha portati | te le ho mandate

examples.tl: La lettera? Gliel'ho data ieri.
examples.en: The letter? I gave it to him yesterday.

examples.tl: I libri me li ha portati Giulia.
examples.en: Giulia brought me the books.

examples.tl: Le foto te le ho mandate stamattina.
examples.en: I sent you the photos this morning.

examples.tl: Che bella notizia! Chi te l'ha detto?
examples.en: What good news! Who told you?

rules.note: The participle looks at the thing only, never at the person who receives: gliel'ho data is right for la lettera whether it went to Marco or to Anna.

rules.rule: A reflexive pair keeps essere, and the participle agrees with the direct pronoun: se l'è messa, me le sono lavate.
rules.pattern: me / te / se + lo / la / li / le + essere + participle agreeing with the thing

examples.tl: Faceva freddo e Luca la giacca se l'è messa subito.
examples.en: It was cold and Luca put his jacket on right away.

examples.tl: Le mani me le sono lavate prima di mangiare.
examples.en: I washed my hands before eating.

examples.tl: Dove sono le chiavi? Me le sono dimenticate a casa.
examples.en: Where are the keys? I left them at home.

rules.note: Luca is a man, but la giacca is feminine, so messa.

rules.rule: Ci (there, or the ci of averci) becomes ce before lo, la, li, le and ne: ce l'ho, ce lo metto, ce n'è, ce ne sono.
rules.pattern: ce + l' / li / le + ho | ce lo / ce la + verb | ce n'è + singular | ce ne sono + plural

examples.tl: Hai la penna? Sì, ce l'ho.
examples.en: Do you have the pen? Yes, I have it.

examples.tl: Hai i biglietti? Sì, ce li ho in borsa.
examples.en: Do you have the tickets? Yes, I have them in my bag.

examples.tl: I bambini a scuola ce li porta il padre.
examples.en: Their father takes the children to school.

examples.tl: C'è ancora pane? Sì, ce n'è molto.
examples.en: Is there still any bread? Yes, there is a lot.

rules.note: Ce n'è with one thing or an amount, ce ne sono with more than one: posti liberi, ce ne sono due. The spelling is ce n'è, never c'è ne.

rules.rule: Before ci (there), mi and ti keep their i and come first: mi ci trovo bene, ti ci porto. The change to me, te happens only before lo, la, li, le, ne.
rules.pattern: mi ci / ti ci + verb | mi ci trovo | ti ci porto | mi ci vogliono dieci minuti

examples.tl: Questa città mi piace e mi ci trovo molto bene.
examples.en: I like this city and I feel very much at home here.

examples.tl: Se vuoi andare al mare, ti ci porto io domenica.
examples.en: If you want to go to the seaside, I'll take you there on Sunday.

examples.tl: Per arrivare in ufficio mi ci vogliono venti minuti.
examples.en: It takes me twenty minutes to get to the office.

rules.note: Level three. Compare ce lo porto (I take it there) with ti ci porto (I take you there).

rules.rule: One + a reflexive verb is ci si + third person singular, because Italian does not say si si: ci si alza, ci si abitua.
rules.pattern: ci si + verb in the third person singular | ci si alza presto | ci si abitua

examples.tl: In vacanza ci si sveglia sempre più tardi.
examples.en: On holiday you always wake up later.

examples.tl: All'inizio è difficile, ma poi ci si abitua.
examples.en: At first it is hard, but then you get used to it.

examples.tl: In questa casa ci si alza presto anche la domenica.
examples.en: In this house people get up early even on Sundays.

rules.note: Level three. This ci replaces the first si; it does not mean us or there.

contrasts.wrong: Mi dai il libro? Sì, lo ti do subito.

right.tl: Mi dai il libro? Sì, te lo do subito.
right.en: Will you give me the book? Yes, I'll give it to you right away.

contrasts.why: English says it to you; Italian puts the person first and the thing second, and ti changes to te before lo: te lo do.

contrasts.wrong: La chiave mi la porta Sara.

right.tl: La chiave me la porta Sara.
right.en: Sara is bringing me the key.

contrasts.why: Before lo, la, li, le and ne, mi cannot keep its i: mi becomes me, so me la porta.

contrasts.wrong: Anna aspetta la risposta: le la mando oggi.

right.tl: Anna aspetta la risposta: gliela mando oggi.
right.en: Anna is waiting for the answer: I'll send it to her today.

contrasts.why: Le (to her) cannot stand before another pronoun. Both gli and le become glie-, in one word with the direct pronoun: gliela, the same form as for a man.

contrasts.wrong: Luca ama i libri: glieli compro due.

right.tl: Luca ama i libri: gliene compro due.
right.en: Luca loves books: I'll buy him two.

contrasts.why: Glieli means all of them to him. With a number after the verb only a part is taken, and a part is ne: gliene compro due.

contrasts.wrong: Il cappotto? Paolo si lo mette subito.

right.tl: Il cappotto? Paolo se lo mette subito.
right.en: His coat? Paolo is putting it on right away.

contrasts.why: Mettersi keeps its reflexive pronoun when the coat becomes lo, and si changes to se before lo: se lo mette.

right.en: I want to tell you tomorrow.

contrasts.why: The two pronouns travel together: both attached to the infinitive (dirtelo) or both before the modal (te lo voglio dire). One on each side is not possible.

right.en: I am coming to give it to you.

contrasts.why: After an infinitive the pair is attached: the infinitive drops its e and all is one word, dartelo. After per no other position is possible.

right.en: The letter? I gave it to him yesterday.

contrasts.why: The l' in gliel'ho is la, for la lettera, and the participle agrees with it: data. Who receives the letter makes no difference.

contrasts.wrong: I libri me l'ha portati Giulia.

right.tl: I libri me li ha portati Giulia.

contrasts.why: Only singular lo and la are shortened to l' before avere. Plural li and le are always written in full: me li ha portati.

contrasts.wrong: Posti liberi? Sì, ci ne sono due.

right.tl: Posti liberi? Sì, ce ne sono due.
right.en: Free seats? Yes, there are two.

contrasts.why: Ci becomes ce before ne, as mi becomes me: ce ne sono. With two seats the verb is plural, sono, not ce n'è.

cheat: Person first, thing second: me lo, te la, ce li, ve le. Never lo mi.
Before lo, la, li, le, ne: mi, ti, ci, vi, si become me, te, ce, ve, se.
To him, to her, to them, formal to you: always glie-, one word: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele, gliene.
A number or an amount after the verb needs ne: me ne dai due, gliene porto un po'.
Infinitive or gerund: attach the pair as one word, dirtelo. With a modal: te lo voglio dire or voglio dirtelo, never split.
Passato prossimo: the participle agrees with the thing, and li, le are never shortened: gliel'ho data, me li ha portati.
Ci before lo, la, li, le, ne is ce: ce l'ho, ce n'è, ce ne sono. Before ci, mi and ti stay: mi ci trovo.
